 Bennett Stirtz needs to justify his role in Thunder's rotation as soon as possible 
 The Thunder have virtually no choice but to play Bennett Stirtz—but he needs to provide more outside shooting nonetheless. By G.C. Bellchamber | Nov 17, 2026, 11:04 AM EST Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source Oct 25, 2026; Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, USA; Oklahoma City Thunder guard Bennett Stirtz (14) walks down the court during the first half at Paycom Center. Mandatory Credit: Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Oklahoma City Thunder have found a way to survive with three of their starters on the sidelines—that alone is a testament to the depth and versatility of this rotation.
--> The Oklahoma City Thunder have found a way to survive with three of their starters on the sidelines—that alone is a testament to the depth and versatility of this rotation.
 But we're still a long way from having things figured out, especially since both Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace are expected to be out, at the very least, for the remainder of the regular season. All three of those recent losses—two against the Portland Trail Blazers and one against the Los Angeles Clippers—serve as evidence of that fact.
--> But we're still a long way from having things figured out, especially since both Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace are expected to be out, at the very least, for the remainder of the regular season. All three of those recent losses—two against the Portland Trail Blazers and one against the Los Angeles Clippers—serve as evidence of that fact.
 And the rest of this season, for Mark Daigneault, is going to present a distinct challenge. What young pieces can he rely on, and how can he tweak the rotation in order to maximize the results and lessen the burden on Shai Gilgeous-Alexander as the campaign wears on?
--> And the rest of this season, for Mark Daigneault, is going to present a distinct challenge. What young pieces can he rely on, and how can he tweak the rotation in order to maximize the results and lessen the burden on Shai Gilgeous-Alexander as the campaign wears on?
 There's no easy answer, although players like Aday Mara and Nique Clifford have provided partial ones.
--> There's no easy answer, although players like Aday Mara and Nique Clifford have provided partial ones.
 But the Thunder's main concern, over the duration of the campaign, needs to be finding the right mix of perimeter shooting and ball-handling to keep this offense playoff viable. In that light, Bennett Stirtz's disappearance over the last four games becomes worrying, and if he's going to justify his guaranteed role in the Thunder's rotation moving forward, he's going to need to start replicating some of what we saw earlier in the season.
--> But the Thunder's main concern, over the duration of the campaign, needs to be finding the right mix of perimeter shooting and ball-handling to keep this offense playoff viable. In that light, Bennett Stirtz's disappearance over the last four games becomes worrying, and if he's going to justify his guaranteed role in the Thunder's rotation moving forward, he's going to need to start replicating some of what we saw earlier in the season.
 Bennett Stirtz doesn't need to be a primary scorer—but he does need to be an offensively viable player
--> Bennett Stirtz doesn't need to be a primary scorer—but he does need to be an offensively viable player
 The Thunder, rather obviously, have weaknesses in both the frontcourt and the backcourt with Holmgren, Williams, and Wallace out for the foreseeable future. But when Holmgren returns, most of the frontcourt will sort itself out.
--> The Thunder, rather obviously, have weaknesses in both the frontcourt and the backcourt with Holmgren, Williams, and Wallace out for the foreseeable future. But when Holmgren returns, most of the frontcourt will sort itself out.
 There's still a potential move for Oklahoma City to make on the wing if they see fit. But with Mara having proved himself as a viable backup big, a rotation of Holmgren, Isaiah Hartenstein, Mara, and Thomas Sorber should be more than adequate in that part of the lineup.
--> There's still a potential move for Oklahoma City to make on the wing if they see fit. But with Mara having proved himself as a viable backup big, a rotation of Holmgren, Isaiah Hartenstein, Mara, and Thomas Sorber should be more than adequate in that part of the lineup.
 The real concern here is the backcourt—especially considering the load that's been put on Gilgeous-Alexander as a playmaker and scorer since Williams and Wallace went down. He's largely been up to the task, averaging 32.8 points, four rebounds, and 4.2 assists while shooting 51.9% from the field over his last five games, but he's looked plainly exhausted in crunch time during that stretch, missing what otherwise would be perfectly makeable shots for the superstar. It's clear he's taken on too great of an offensive workload, and even a string of solid performances from Ajay Mitchell isn't enough to fully relieve that pressure.
--> The real concern here is the backcourt—especially considering the load that's been put on Gilgeous-Alexander as a playmaker and scorer since Williams and Wallace went down. He's largely been up to the task, averaging 32.8 points, four rebounds, and 4.2 assists while shooting 51.9% from the field over his last five games, but he's looked plainly exhausted in crunch time during that stretch, missing what otherwise would be perfectly makeable shots for the superstar. It's clear he's taken on too great of an offensive workload, and even a string of solid performances from Ajay Mitchell isn't enough to fully relieve that pressure.
 Stirtz, obviously, isn't going to suddenly develop into a primary scorer for the Thunder. But having players in the backcourt, especially those with both perimeter-shooting and ball-handling pedigrees, is going to be paramount for Oklahoma City moving forward. In theory, Stirtz should be one of those pieces —even if there's something to be given up on the defensive end when he takes on extensive minutes.
--> Stirtz, obviously, isn't going to suddenly develop into a primary scorer for the Thunder. But having players in the backcourt, especially those with both perimeter-shooting and ball-handling pedigrees, is going to be paramount for Oklahoma City moving forward. In theory, Stirtz should be one of those pieces —even if there's something to be given up on the defensive end when he takes on extensive minutes.
 But over his last three games, Stirtz has all but disappeared from the Thunder offense. In that span, he's averaged just 3.7 points, one rebound, and one assist while shooting 30% from beyond the arc. And although his minutes have seen a sharp decrease from where he was at earlier in the season, he still averaged 18 minutes per game across those three outings.
--> But over his last three games, Stirtz has all but disappeared from the Thunder offense. In that span, he's averaged just 3.7 points, one rebound, and one assist while shooting 30% from beyond the arc. And although his minutes have seen a sharp decrease from where he was at earlier in the season, he still averaged 18 minutes per game across those three outings.
 If the team were fully healthy, perhaps this sort of play would force Daigneault to take a step back and pull Stirtz out of the rotation for a few games—give him some time to reset and to clear his head. But with the position the Thunder are in, they simply don't have the luxury of doing that. Stirtz needs to play, at the very least, probably 12-15 minutes per night moving forward.
--> If the team were fully healthy, perhaps this sort of play would force Daigneault to take a step back and pull Stirtz out of the rotation for a few games—give him some time to reset and to clear his head. But with the position the Thunder are in, they simply don't have the luxury of doing that. Stirtz needs to play, at the very least, probably 12-15 minutes per night moving forward.
 And he's shown, especially in the early parts of the season, that those minutes can be productive. He's a capable catch-and-shoot scorer, and he has enough ball-handling juice to operate as a complementary facilitator from time to time with the bench unit.
--> And he's shown, especially in the early parts of the season, that those minutes can be productive. He's a capable catch-and-shoot scorer, and he has enough ball-handling juice to operate as a complementary facilitator from time to time with the bench unit.
 Perhaps Nikola Topic provides some sort of insurance, or the arrival of Clifford helps negate some of the need for Stirtz's shooting in the rotation.
--> Perhaps Nikola Topic provides some sort of insurance, or the arrival of Clifford helps negate some of the need for Stirtz's shooting in the rotation.
 But if those looks don't start to fall more consistently, and Daigneault continues to allow Stirtz to be sidelined within Oklahoma City's offensive structure, the Thunder will have lost a helpful component of their backcourt. 
--> But if those looks don't start to fall more consistently, and Daigneault continues to allow Stirtz to be sidelined within Oklahoma City's offensive structure, the Thunder will have lost a helpful component of their backcourt. 
 In short, Stirtz is likely going to see minutes no matter what—he simply needs to get back to his game in order to justify that opportunity.
